- **#603 OPEN 2026-07-28 (CC-C; surfaced + measured by B-COST-ACCOUNTING-HONESTY, §9.4-homed at close) — SLIPPAGE CONFLATES *SIGNAL STALENESS* WITH *EXECUTION COST*; THE PEROLD SPLIT NEEDS AN ARRIVAL PRICE WE DO NOT PERSIST.** Entry slippage is measured as `(fillPrice − intendedPrice) × qty` where `intendedPrice = signal.entryPrice` — the price at the moment the SIGNAL was generated. That single number therefore contains TWO economically different things: **delay cost** (the market drifting between the decision and the order being placed) and **trading cost** (what it actually costs to get filled). The standard decomposition is Perold (1988) implementation shortfall — `delay = (P_arrival − P_decision)×filled`, `trading = (P_exec − P_arrival)×filled` — and it requires an **ARRIVAL price** (best ask at order placement), which we do NOT persist today. **MEASURED (live, at B-COST-ACCOUNTING-HONESTY close):** mean |intended−actual| entry gap **0.278%** — plausible execution slippage — but **24 closed trades exceed 1%** and the max is **8.771%**. A fill 8.8% better than intended is not a venue phenomenon; that is the signal price going stale before we act on it. Today the two are indistinguishable, so we cannot tell a signal-timeliness problem from an execution problem. **NOT a defect in the current accounting** — B-COST-ACCOUNTING-HONESTY left the fill prices (and therefore the net P&L) exactly right; this is a MEASUREMENT capability we lack. **SCOPE:** capture + persist the arrival price at the order-placement seam (the book snapshot already exists there), then report delay vs trading cost separately. ⚠️ If per-component numbers are ever reported, state WHICH convention — the Kissell/Wagner and CFA forms are identical in total but attribute differently between the delay and opportunity buckets. **HOME (§9.4): its own batch `B-IMPLEMENTATION-SHORTFALL`, owner CC-C, sequenced after the ACTIVE_PATH_FLOW bring-up.** Related: B-COST-ACCOUNTING-HONESTY (completion report §out-of-scope), #583 (xStock timing/liquidity — a signal-staleness measure would inform it). **OPEN (homed).**

CI went **GREEN** anyway. **THE HOLE:** `scripts/check-tsc-baseline.mjs` grades against a frozen baseline (585 errors) and evidently dedups such that a NEW `TS2339` in a file that ALREADY carries baselined `TS2339`s (here `vts-runner.ts` has pre-existing `OpenVirtualTrade` phantom reads at `:3306/:3399/:3405/:5626`…) is absorbed as not-new. ⇒ **a real new type error is invisible to CI in any file already holding a baselined error of that code.** **COMPOUNDING (CC-A's own verification also masked, recorded honestly):** the local check was `npx tsc | grep -E 'vts-runner|error TS' | head -20` — the client baseline errors filled the first 20 lines and `head -20` truncated the vts-runner errors, so 'type-clean' was a truncation artifact. Same sampling-blindness class as the `fsck|head`, the D-5 ref check, the '3 vs 29 instances' miss. **WHY IT MATTERS:** CI's TypeScript gate is one of the four green-required checks; this hole let a genuine bucket-1 defect reach the review branch under a green light. It does not corrupt anything (the frozen-baseline design was a deliberate #-of-errors-freeze, per `ci.yml:25-29`), but it weakens the gate's guarantee. **CANDIDATE FIX (not built; Langston to rule scope):** key the baseline dedup on `(file, line-context/message)` or `(file, code, symbol)` rather than `(file, code)`, OR require per-file error COUNT not to increase. Either makes a new same-code error visible. **VERIFICATION METHOD LESSON (applies now):** verify tsc by reading the FULL untruncated `grep '<file>'` output and confirming the EDITED line numbers appear in zero errors — never `head`-limited, never trusting green CI on a file with a baselined error of the same code. **HOME:** its own item — **Langston-routed to owner CC-B 2026-07-25** ("gets its own home, not a footnote… systemic gate hole"); CC-B to confirm ownership + name the target batch/phase (CC-A surfaced it but is on #558, and this is CI/governance-tooling). Related: #558 A0, `check-tsc-baseline.mjs`, `.tsc-baseline.json`, rule 13/#568 (absent-as-valid). **★ RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (B-TSC-BASELINE-FIX, CC-B, head `a587408bd`, cold CI 4/4 green run `30298671677`, Langston-approved, API-verified):** replaced the per-(file,code) COUNT gate with a **(file, code, MESSAGE)-identity** gate — a new error carries a distinct message so it's caught regardless of (file,code) headroom, AND catches the 1-for-1 swap a count gate misses (the case that steered Langston to approach A over a no-headroom count invariant). Verification (two red cold-CI runs — the gate proving itself) surfaced + fixed three deeper reliability holes so identity is deterministic + host-portable: (1) `--incremental false` — tsc cache non-determinism (stale post-pull buildinfo reported 401 vs true 394; 43 baseline identities were cache-artifacts); (2) `<ROOT>` path canonicalization — tsc embeds host-specific absolute paths in messages (`C:/DawnTraderV3-new/…` vs `/home/runner/work/…`) → 9 false regressions cross-host; (3) `--noErrorTruncation` + 300-char clip — tsc truncates long types at a char budget that includes host-varying path lengths → different truncation point per host (2 drizzle `TS2741`s). Baseline regenerated: 394/48, message-keyed, **0 absolute paths**, 64KB. Test 6/6 incl. a Windows/Linux/analyst portability case. All normalization runs identically at generate+compare and erases only host-varying prefix/tail → can only under-normalize (loud false regression), never hide a real error. Full record: `Claude Comms and Packages/Batch Completion/B_TSC_BASELINE_FIX_COMPLETION_REPORT.md`. **RESOLVED.**

On a tree with three concurrent sessions it can, and did.** My attestation ("index read before commit") was **TRUE and still produced a clobber** — which means the attestation cannot detect this failure mode at all. ⚠️ **And the path-limited form that WOULD be atomic (`git commit -- <paths>`) is exactly the one rule 25 documents as SEGFAULTING on the GDrive FUSE mount (#542) — which is *why* the attested bare form exists.** So the two rules interlock into a genuine gap: the safe form crashes, and the working form races. **INTERIM MITIGATION (adopt immediately, both other sessions too):** put the add, the index read, and the commit in **ONE shell invocation** so the window is microseconds rather than seconds — and **re-read `git show --stat <sha>` AFTER committing**, because that is the only check that can actually catch this (I found it that way). A post-commit stat is not optional on a shared tree. **★ RECURRENCE CONTEXT, recorded against my own interest:** I flagged this exact hazard TO ANALYST ~4 hours earlier when I noticed their files staged under me, and then walked into it myself. **A discipline that its own author violates within one session is evidence the mechanism is missing, not that the author was careless** — the same conclusion P19-B8.5f reached about hand-maintained field lists (an assertion list is itself the object that fails; use the compiler). **HOME (§9.4): `B-SHARED-TREE-COMMIT-ATOMICITY` — owner CC-B, and it needs Langston's ruling on whether the real fix is per-session worktrees (which would end the shared index entirely) rather than a tighter procedure.** Related: #540 (the procedure this gap is in), #542 (the segfault that forced the bare form), #545. **OPEN (homed, mitigation stated).** **★★ RULED 2026-07-22 — WORKTREES, not the private index (Langston; he marked his footing plainly as RULED ON REPORTED FACT, since he cannot reach the Windows tree and did not re-run the test).** **THE DECIDING EVIDENCE (CC-B ran the test Langston's wedged mount blocked):** `git worktree add --detach <scratch> HEAD` from the shared GDrive repo **succeeded in 10.6s**, checked out all **5,239** files; the new worktree's `git status --porcelain` was **EMPTY** and `git ls-files` returned **5,239** ⇒ **the index is initialised from HEAD BY CONSTRUCTION.** Removal + prune left the main repo untouched. **★ And the strongest evidence was not the test: `git worktree list` shows TWO worktrees ALREADY LIVE on this repo** (`.claude/worktrees/agent-ae6af331`, `wizardly-einstein`) — the mechanism is already in use here, not a proposal. **WHY IT BEATS THE PRIVATE INDEX (the spike Analyst ran — `B-SPIKE-PER-SESSION-INDEX`):** both isolate equally well, but the private index requires a `read-tree HEAD` first, and **omitting it commits a tree that DELETES every tracked file — while an empty private index is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a legitimately-empty one, so nothing warns you** (Langston's find). ⇒ it converts a race into a silent catastrophic footgun guarded only by memory. **A worktree has no such step, so there is nothing to forget.** **⚠️ SCOPE OF THE TEST, stated because conflating the two mounts would be a false generalisation:** this proves worktrees on the **CC-side Windows Google Drive mount**, NOT on Langston's **Helsinki rclone FUSE mount** (`/mnt/gdrive`) — different driver, different failure modes. It happens not to matter for #557 (the shared-index race is between the three CC sessions on the Windows tree, exactly what was tested) but this must NOT later be cited as "worktrees are proven on GDrive" unqualified. **INTERIM, until worktrees are adopted:** the two mitigations stand — single-invocation add+verify+commit, and **`git show --stat <sha>` AFTER every commit**, which is the only check that can catch this by construction. **NEXT: the adoption batch under `B-SHARED-TREE-COMMIT-ATOMICITY` (per-session worktree + the roster binding a session to its tree).**

- **#540 STANDING RULE (amended 2026-07-19, Langston-ruled; guard v2 = `.claude/hooks/guard-bare-commit.mjs`, mechanical): SHARED-TREE COMMIT DISCIPLINE — three tiers, each with its OWN attestation; the staged INDEX is part of the wrench.** **TIER 1 — ROUTINE (default, no token):** `git status` index check → stage explicit paths → `git commit -F <msg> -- <paths>`. NOTE (#542): this form segfaults intermittently on the mount; a segfault moves you to Tier 2, it does not license improvisation. **TIER 2 — MOUNT SEGFAULT (token, index-verified attestation):** run `git diff --cached --name-only`; EVERY listed path must be yours (another session's path present → STOP, resolve in-channel). Then `CC_COMMIT_ATTESTED=1 git commit -F <msg>` (bare). **The token here attests exactly: "I ran the staged-set check and every path is mine."** It is justified by that typed attestation ALONE — NOT by bare-form reliability (#542 owns the mount data; the two rails stay separate). **TIER 3 — INDEX CORRUPTION / REPAIR (token, protocol attestation — a DIFFERENT claim):** the index check is impossible here, so the token does NOT mean "index verified." It attests exactly: **"stale-lock protocol satisfied, repairing."** Stale-lock protocol (ALL three, else WAIT): (a) a git operation reports the lock blocking; (b) no live git process exists (process-list check); (c) the lock's mtime is frozen across a ≥60s recheck. Repair set (never blocked by the guard, listed in the hook): `git reset` (mixed), `rm .git/index` for rebuild, `git fsck`, `git write-tree` (diagnostic). Branch-moving plumbing (`commit-tree`, `update-ref` → HEAD/refs/heads/*) requires the token even in repair. **The token name is deliberately tier-neutral: `CC_COMMIT_ATTESTED` asserts only "the applicable tier protocol was run"; WHICH protocol is stated in-channel. EVERY token use posts an in-channel statement NAMING THE TIER whose protocol was run** — always, not only when the tree is shared-active. A Tier-3 action stated as Tier-2 is a false attestation (the appearance-of-control defect one layer down). **Guard v2 blocks:** bare `git commit`, `git commit -a`, `git commit-tree`, `git update-ref` targeting HEAD or refs/heads/*, `rm` of `.git/index.lock`. **The token opens each EXCEPT `-a`, which has NO sanctioned escape by construction:** `-a` stages tracked modifications AT COMMIT TIME — after the `git diff --cached` the token attests — so a token on `-a` would be a signed statement about an index the command then changes underneath it, laundering an unreviewed sweep as an audited one. The retired name `CC_INDEX_VERIFIED` FAILS CLOSED (cannot linger as an undocumented second door). **Plumbing commits are prohibited for routine use — enforced mechanically, not by convention.** The write-tree/commit-tree/update-ref commit bypass used on 2026-07-19 (1ac6e96f5) is RETIRED as of this amendment. Guard v2's block-coverage of the plumbing shapes must be TESTED (run the hook against each shape, confirm it fires) before this text lands — no asserted absence of holes. The test matrix MUST include the near-miss pair: the guard FIRES on `rm .git/index.lock` (token-gated) and does NOT fire on `rm .git/index` (repair, never-blocked) — proving the match is not over-broad, not merely that it fires. **KNOWN PROPERTY — FAIL-OPEN (stated as a property, not a defect):** the guard is fail-open by design — any payload it cannot parse is PERMITTED (a hook that hard-fails on malformed payloads would break every session, a worse failure). Consequence: a green test run is only as trustworthy as its payloads are well-formed (the 2026-07-19 first test run proved this — invalid harness JSON made a live block read as dead). Test harnesses against this hook must validate their own payload JSON before trusting a result. **Provenance:** original #540 (08f89ed78) + the 2026-07-19 guard-token ruling thread; sweeps d090178d6 / 5f291a17e; mount data #542; EOL policy #539.

- **#349 — TEC config staleness fence latches-until-restart + freezes the whole VTS cycle (B-NEW-40 soak finding, CC-A 2026-06-25). ✅ RESOLVED 2026-06-25 by batch B-TEC-SELFHEAL** (Kyle-greenlit; full 11-step workflow, Langston Step-1/2/4 APPROVED, CI 4-green run 28181014927, deployed staging restart#417 HTTP 200, all 4 TEC classes fresh + zero TEC_STALE_FAIL_CLOSED post-deploy). **Fix shipped:** OBJ-1 = the lazy-refresh trigger relocated to a single-call-site helper at the TOP of `resolveTECConfig` (before both throws) so a stale-past-ceiling consult schedules its own coalesced refresh and self-heals in ~1 cycle (was: latch-until-restart); OBJ-2 = per-trade try/catch in the VTS exit loop (mirror `paper-execution-engine.ts:794`) so one stale-class trade no longer aborts the whole cycle. Fail-closed fence byte-identical (the safety property is preserved — OBJ-5(c)). **Unprimed-class delta (Langston Step-4 note):** the new `!tecConfigCache.has` guard ALSO removed a prior incidental behavior — an unprimed class no longer schedules a (pointless) refresh before `TEC_CACHE_MISS_FATAL`; correct, since boot hard-fail means a live process never has an unprimed class. **OBJ-5 real-world close:** deterministic self-heal proven by the 48-test TEC suite; the latch-vs-self-heal real-world proof is the 06-28 xStock weekend reopen — scheduled §10.5 verification alert (`tec_selfheal_verify`, fires 06-29 06:00 UTC) confirms it self-heals vs the old 17h cascade. **OBJ-3 considered-and-declined stands (below).** _(Diagnosis history retained below.)_ ★ **DEEPER ROOT (confirmed CC-A + Langston 2026-06-25, supersedes the cold-cache-at-reopen framing below):** the reopen staleness is one TRIGGER of a general defect — the fail-closed fence is CORRECT and stays, but (1) the staleness THROW (`resolveTECConfig` ~:248) is BEFORE the lazy refresh trigger (~:271) so the cache can never self-heal — it latches until a process restart (no periodic refresh exists); and (2) the VTS exit loop (`vts-runner.ts:2421`) has no per-trade try/catch, so one stale-class open trade aborts the WHOLE multi-class cycle (exit-mgmt FIRST at `:3273` before scan/open at `:3293` → opens blocked too). Live proof: 06-22 reopen stuck ~17h continuous until a deploy restart; crypto_spot also stuck ~5h (not weekend-only). The fix = **B-TEC-SELFHEAL**: OBJ-1 fire the refresh through the coalescer before the throw (self-heal in ~1 cycle); OBJ-2 per-trade exit-loop isolation (mirror the already-correct `paper-execution-engine.ts:794`). The reopen-warm framing (below) is DROPPED — self-heal is general. **★ OBJ-3 (bounded periodic re-warm timer) — CONSIDERED-AND-DECLINED (Langston Step-1, 2026-06-25):** OBJ-1+OBJ-2 are the complete root fix; a timer would only suppress one correct-by-design transient throw for a zero-consumer class, at the cost of an always-on singleton + new failure surface on a mode-shared safety path (gold-plating; NO-PATCHES cuts toward minimal). **Conditional reopen trigger:** B-TEC-SELFHEAL OBJ-5 must observe a zero-consumer class self-healing within ~1 cycle; IF staging ever shows that first-consult blip is MATERIAL on the active/paper path (real open positions), OBJ-3 reopens as a named follow-up. _(Original soak-finding detail retained below for the record.)_ The B-NEW-40 14-day soak verification (alert `b83b1e4b`, run 2026-06-25 against deploy-ts 2026-05-17) returned **FAIL on its presence-check** (3754 raw `TEC_STALE_FAIL_CLOSED` log lines ≈ ~1877 distinct incidents, clustered on just 3 days: 2026-06-15 / 06-22 / 06-23, then STOPPED — nothing since). **BUT the failure mode B-NEW-40 actually fixed did NOT recur:** pool/socket errors = **0** over 38.9 days (pg-pool keepalive held). The stale events are a DIFFERENT, narrower cause: **`assetClass=xstock_spot`, cache age ~25h, "Refusing to honor a stale kill-switch snapshot,"** every one *contained* inside a VTS cycle (`[ITEM4][VTS] Cycle error (contained)`) — so zero live impact while active trading is OFF. **Root mechanism — CORRECTED 2026-06-25 (Kyle architectural context + CC-A code-confirmation; supersedes the initial "VTS consults during the close" read):** VTS does NOT consult `xstock_spot` during the weekend close — it is correctly PAUSED. xStock runs a weekend shutdown 8PM Fri→8PM Sun ET (`market-hours.ts:79-85` `isInXstockWeekendClose`; poll-reconciled by `session-lifecycle-controller.ts` since the B-NEW-52 cron retirement): at shutdown `runWeekendShutdownCore` calls `xstockSpotScanner.pause()` + suspends open trades; the VTS per-pair eval also returns early on `!isXstockMarketOpenUTC` (`eval-cycle.ts:312-314`) BEFORE any TEC consult. So nothing consults the xStock TEC config all weekend. The TEC config cache is primed ONLY at boot (`primeTECConfig()`, `server/index.ts:815`) and otherwise lazy-on-consult (`trailing-exit-controller.ts:160`). **The staleness is therefore a COLD-CACHE-AT-REOPEN, not a during-close-consult bug:** across the weekend pause the config goes stale (un-consulted), and at Sunday 8PM ET reopen — when `runWeekendRestartCore` resumes the scanner — the FIRST consults fail-closed on the stale config until the lazy refresh lands. **Timing corroborates:** the 06-15 / 06-22 clusters are at ~00:00 UTC = Sun 20:00 ET = the reopen edge (events tick once/min with cache-age growing +60000ms, i.e. one class failing repeatedly until the refresh catches up). The weekend pre-warm (`runWeekendRestartCore:430` `runPrewarmWithCircuitBreaker`) refreshes the OHLC **price** snapshot at reopen but does **NOT** re-prime the TEC **config** snapshot — that is the exact gap. **Live state 2026-06-25 also confirms:** the two TRADED spot classes (`crypto_spot`/`xstock_spot`) are fresh (consulted every ~60s); the two PERP classes (`crypto_perp`/`xstock_perp`) sit stale-by-ceiling (~11.4h, since the last restart) with `consecutiveFailCount=0` — **benign: nothing consults perps (we trade spot only), so they legitimately aren't refreshed; no fence fires for them.** **Why this matters:** harmless now (VTS-contained), but when xStock active-trading turns ON (Phase 19), a stale `xstock_spot` kill-switch snapshot would fail-CLOSE and BLOCK xStock trades during/after every market-closed gap.

**Refresh internals (CC-A read `refreshTECConfigForClass` @ `trailing-exit-controller.ts:361`):** the refresh pulls ONLY DB `module_constants` rows (break_even_enabled, trigger_r, target_lock_r, trail_distance, …) — **pure config, ZERO live-market-data dependency** — so warming it is cheap and has no venue dependency (it works fine even with the market closed). This is what makes the reopen-warm fix below trivial and correct.

**ROOT FORK — RESOLVED 2026-06-25 (Kyle context + CC-A code + Langston/NEW Claude concur):** the earlier open question ("should VTS consult `xstock_spot` during a closed window?") is answered **NO and it doesn't** — VTS is correctly paused for the whole close (scanner pause + `eval-cycle.ts:312-314` early-return). So there is no closed-window consult to gate, no continuous 24/7 keep-warm timer to build, and NEW Claude's reorg owes nothing on this sub-line (Langston confirmed the reorg-homed fork closes clean). The problem is purely the **reopen edge**.

**FIX [Phase-19, scoped + simple]:** extend the EXISTING Sunday-reopen hook — `runWeekendRestartCore` (`session-lifecycle-controller.ts:417-465`), which already runs the OHLC price pre-warm at `:430` — to ALSO re-prime the TEC **config** for the resuming xStock class(es) at reopen (call `primeTECConfig()` / the per-class equivalent, exactly as boot does at `server/index.ts:815`). This is the §11-blessed **cold-start-warmup-at-resumption** pattern Kyle explicitly endorses; it mirrors what the price snapshot already does. **NOT** a new always-on timer, and **NOT** extending the 300000ms ceiling (that would weaken the fail-closed fence — §11-prohibited; the fence is behaving correctly). Tiny additional guard worth a line: warming runs even though the venue is closed, which is fine because the refresh is pure DB config (no live-data dependency, confirmed above). _(This supersedes the earlier "continuous keep-warm timer + derived-interval + self-pruning-membership" design — that machinery is unnecessary once the cause is pinned to the reopen edge rather than a continuous gap.)_

> Source: `Scope Files/B_LANGSTON_QUEUE_SCOPE.md` §6. Engine `comms-infra/discord/langston_queue.py` (39 unit tests) + `discord-langston-bridge.py` wiring; self-advance behind `LANGSTON_SELF_ADVANCE` (currently OFF). Langston Step-4 APPROVED 2026-06-22; his two findings (enqueue-too-broad, missing-marker-dead-locks-loop) FIXED + pushed (da02616d2). Live shakeout 2026-06-22 PASSED on those two + core auto-advance; surfaced the two gaps below.

- **#342 — B-LANGSTON-QUEUE OBJ-3 circle-back un-block NOT implemented (live-shakeout finding, 2026-06-22).** The *parking* half of skip-and-circle works (a blocked item is set aside, the loop skips it), but NOTHING flips a `blocked` item back to `ready` when its `want` dependency lands — and the marker grammar has no `ready` status. So a parked item stalls until manually re-marked; OBJ-3's "circle back the moment the dependency lands" is inert. Degrades safely (the item just waits, surfaced by the LOUD park notice), so it is a completeness gap, not a hazard — but B-LANGSTON-QUEUE is NOT fully functional until this lands (§9.1). **Proposed fix (Langston reviewing):** add `[[QUEUE id=X status=ready]]` so a CC (or Langston) can un-park when the dependency lands; optionally also auto-flip when a CC posts referencing the id. **HOME: B-LANGSTON-QUEUE go-live increment (Langston-reviewed Step-4 diff before flipping `LANGSTON_SELF_ADVANCE=1` for real).** **OPEN.**
- **#345 — B-LANGSTON-QUEUE: a real-inbound review gets ONE degraded self-advance re-pass (first live-use finding, 2026-06-22).** When a CC posts a review request, the bridge enqueues it (summary truncated to 500 chars, `pointer=None`) AND invokes Langston on the FULL message — but the real-inbound invocation prompt does NOT instruct the queue marker, so his first (complete) review carries no `done` marker → the item stays `ready` → the self-advance loop re-feeds it ONCE, now from the truncated summary with no pointer → Langston posts a shallower re-take (he flagged the truncation himself), emits the marker, item→done. Not a loop/hazard (it self-completes), but every review currently costs one wasted, degraded re-pass + a confusing shallow channel post. **Two fixes: (A root) append the queue-marker instruction to the real-inbound invocation when the message enqueued an item, so the FIRST review marks it done and there is NO re-pass; (B) capture a `pointer` at enqueue (regex an inbox/file path or commit sha out of the message) so any re-feed isn't degraded.** Surfaced on the build-crew-blueprint review (item `1518653167796097095`). **HOME: a small B-LANGSTON-QUEUE follow-up increment (Langston-reviewed). OPEN.**
  - **★ ESCALATED 2026-06-24 — the same defect, under sustained crew chatter, became an actual re-feed loop, and self-advance is now TEMPORARILY DISABLED.** During the B-ALERT batch's heavy CC↔Langston traffic, the `ready` conversational items (CC replies that START with "Langston", enqueued because `is_review_request` matched) were re-fed repeatedly, making Langston re-review already-settled topics over and over. **NEW root-cause finding (C):** the two-tier `CapTracker` runaway-brake **resets on every real Kyle/CC inbound** (`process_task`: `if not task.get("self_advance"): _cap.reset()`), so with continuous inbound the same-id halt NEVER accumulated to 2 → a stuck (ready, never-`done`) item re-fired indefinitely (observed: item `1519109514383720469` re-invoked at 22:56/22:57/23:01). **Stopgap applied 2026-06-24:** removed the systemd drop-in (`LANGSTON_SELF_ADVANCE` OFF, `daemon-reload` + restart) + cleared the 9-item ready backlog (marked `done`). Langston still answers DIRECT messages; only the auto-pickup is paused. **#345's fix now has THREE parts:** (A) append the queue-marker instruction to the real-inbound invocation so the FIRST review marks it done; (B) capture a `pointer` at enqueue; **(C) gate enqueue to GENUINE review-requests only (not conversational "Langston —" replies) AND make the same-id cap survive inbound resets (e.g. track same-id re-fires independently of the distinct-advance reset).** Re-enable `LANGSTON_SELF_ADVANCE=1` only after #345 ships Langston-reviewed. SIM "Langston self-advance loop" entry updated to the disabled state.
  - **✅ RESOLVED 2026-06-24 (B-LANGSTON-QUEUE-345, CC-A, deployed `907cd93db`).** All three fixes shipped + Langston Step-4 APPROVED: **C1** the enqueue gate now requires a review-REQUEST verb (`_REQUEST_VERB_RE`), so a discussion reply that merely says "verified/agreed" no longer enqueues (the bare-`verif` over-match is gone); **OBJ-B** a re-fetchable pointer (inbox path/repo file/sha) is captured at enqueue; **OBJ-A** the bridge auto-settles an enqueued item on any reply — `done` if Langston actually reviewed it, else a new `noop` terminal status (never falsely `done`) — so no degraded re-pass; **C2** a per-ITEM `self_advance_refires` counter persisted across save/load (Langston Step-4 caught a real persist bug — the increment was mutate-not-saved → the halt could never trip; fixed + an integration test that round-trips save/load now guards it). 79/79 unit tests. **Live shakeout PASSED:** self-advance re-enabled, a conversational probe containing "verified" did NOT enqueue (0 ready), zero churn re-invokes since re-enable. `LANGSTON_SELF_ADVANCE=1` is back on. SIM self-advance entry updated to the re-enabled state. **RESOLVED.**
- **#344 — B-LANGSTON-QUEUE: a marker-carrying CONTROL inbound was enqueued as a phantom work-item (shakeout-2 finding, 2026-06-22). ✅ FIXED same-day.** In shakeout-2 the un-park message ("Langston — `[[QUEUE id=UP1 status=ready]]` … please re-review") tripped `is_review_request` (it says "re-review") and got enqueued as a NEW item, which the loop then fed back to Langston (who correctly refused to confabulate a review of an unknown item). Fix: the enqueue gate also requires `not lq.marker_attempted(prompt)` — an inbound carrying a `[[QUEUE …]]` marker is a CONTROL message (un-park/re-mark), not a fresh review request. Tests 54→56. **HOME: folded into the go-live increment. RESOLVED (pending Langston quick-confirm + push).**
- **#343 — B-LANGSTON-QUEUE marker parser brittle to UNQUOTED want/reason (live-shakeout finding, 2026-06-22).** The `[[QUEUE …]]` regex requires `want="…"` / `reason="…"` to be QUOTED. In the shakeout Langston naturally emitted `want=shakeout-artifact` (unquoted) → the whole marker failed to parse → it fell through to the FINDING-2 park-unmarked path (so a genuine `blocked` was misclassified as "no marker"). Degraded SAFELY (loud park, nothing lost), but a stateless LLM will sometimes omit quotes. **Proposed fix (Langston reviewing): loosen the capture to accept an unquoted single token OR a quoted multi-word value for want/reason.** **HOME: same B-LANGSTON-QUEUE go-live increment as #342.** **OPEN.**

First trade to call `initializeTrailingState` sets the shared `currentStopPrice` + `originalStopPrice` + `highWaterMark`; subsequent trades inherit those values and the engine evaluates ALL of them against the FIRST trade's stop. When any one trade closes, `clearTrailingState(symbol)` (vts-runner.ts:2500, paper-execution-engine.ts:1352) wipes the shared state — next exit-cycle re-initializes from whichever surviving trade iterates first, so remaining trades on the symbol now follow a totally different trade's geometry. **Real-world impact:** displayed `trade.stopLoss` and engine `currentStopPrice` diverge for any trade after the first one on a given symbol. UI shows the trade's own per-trade stop; engine evaluates against the shared state's stop. Trades stay alive past their displayed stops (FET/USD range_trade in 2026-05-13 CSV: displayed stop 0.22863, engine stop 0.2117, current 0.225 → below displayed but above engine → still alive after 58h). BE-latch / target-latch / moonbag fires on one trade's geometry but the new floor applies to ALL concurrent trades on the symbol. Trailing HWM is conflated across trades. **Crypto duplicate-guard caps at 1 per (symbol, strategy) but allows different strategies → bug manifests in `quant-strong_trend` lane (vwap_pullback + strong_bull_trend co-eligible) and across regime transitions.** Active trading paper/live have no per-symbol cap → bug applies equally. **Fix proposal (B-NEW-24 / BATCH_80):** key `trailingStates` by trade.id (or positionId for paper/live). Plumb tradeId through `TECUpdate`. Update all reads + writes (getTrailingState, clearTrailingState, persistence migration). Recommend collapsing `trade.stopLoss` and `engine.currentStopPrice` into a single source of truth (UI Option C: display always = engine trigger). Needs full workflow with Langston design review BEFORE implementation per NO PATCHES doctrine (CLAUDE.md §5 #15). ### #947 OPEN 2026-08-29 (CC-INFRA, found when Kyle asked why B-TOKEN-WATCH's change-class was undecided) — THIRTEEN SCOPE FILES DECLARE A CHANGE-CLASS THE CHECKER CANNOT READ, BECAUSE ITS PATTERN IS LINE-ANCHORED

`CHANGE_CLASS_MARKER` (`scripts/governance-checker/config.mjs:180`) begins with a line anchor followed by optional list markers, so a declaration is only seen at the START of a line. **But the house style for a scope header is one line carrying several fields** — `**Batch:** X · **Created:** Y · **change-class:** non_architecture` — and a mid-line declaration never matches.

⛔ **MEASURED over all 326 scope files, and the population matters because my first diagnosis was wrong:**
- **13 files carry a REAL declaration the anchor rejects.** 8 declare `non_architecture` and are therefore graded against the STRICTER `architecture` doc-set, so they are flagged for missing `SYSTEM_MANUAL`/`SIM` entries they do not owe. 4 declare `architecture` (graded the same either way, still flagged). 1 declares `auditable`.
- **3 files merely MENTION the phrase in prose** and declare nothing. **Correctly unparsed — not part of this defect**, and the reason the raw count of 17 is not the finding.

⚠️ **MY FIRST CAUSE WAS WRONG AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE SHAPE RECURS.** My own scope used `**change-class:**` — colon INSIDE the bold — and the pattern wants it outside. I generalised that to all 17. **A candidate regex tolerant of asterisks fixed 2 and left 11**, which is what sent me back to look. The colon is a real second cause affecting a couple of files; **the line anchor is the cause for the large majority.** `wrong-object`: a mechanism that explained MY case, asserted over a population I had not checked.

✅ **ALREADY DONE, and it is the whole of what I was entitled to do alone:** my two scope files (`B_TOKEN_WATCH_SCOPE.md`, `B_CREW_STATUS_2_SCOPE.md`) are reformatted to `**change-class**: ` and both now parse as `non_architecture`, verified by running the checker's own regex against the files.

⛔ **WHY I DID NOT FIX THE REGEX OR THE OTHER 11 FILES.** The regex governs how EVERY batch is graded, so relaxing it re-grades other sessions' closed batches — 8 would move from the strict set to the one they declared, which changes what their close required. That is not a change one session makes to another's governance record without the owner. **And a naive de-anchoring is actively dangerous: three files mention `change-class` in prose, so a looser pattern must still not match a sentence.** The safe fix needs the prose cases as its negative control.

⇒ **HOME: `B-GOV-CLASS-PARSE`, owner CC-A (the B-GOV series owns `scripts/governance-checker/`), placed in `PHASE_19_PLAN` at the governance-tooling tail, after the existing B-GOV items.** No date — the queue in front of it moves.

★ **NOT a defect, checked and cleared:** an invalid class fails CLOSED — `readDeclaredClass` returns `DEFAULT_CLASS` with `reason: invalid-class:<x>`, which is the correct behaviour and is why `auditable` is not a second bug.

### #946 OPEN 2026-08-29 (CC-A) — ⛔ LANGSTON’S `MEMORY.md` IS **2× ITS CAP**, AND THE PARTS THAT LOOK LOAD-BEARING **ALREADY EXCEED IT ON THEIR OWN**

**MEASURED at `/home/langston/MEMORY.md`, summing encoded line bytes: 49,224 B against the 24,576 B cap in `CLAUDE.md` §3.2 — over by 24,648, almost exactly double.** 202 lines, 70 blank. **The 25 heaviest lines carry 44% of the file.**

**SECTION BREAKDOWN (largest first):** STANDING NOTES 9,598 (19%) · governance-integrity program 5,278 (11%) · **retractions 5,214 (11%)** · CURRENT STATE 4,156 (8%) · `F-G-1` **(OPEN)** 3,804 (8%) · `B-MISTAKES-FILE` **(closed)** 3,376 · `B-CONDUCT-FILE` **(closed)** 2,665 · `P19-B-PERPFEED` **(closed)** 2,482 · `B-MBIM-SWITCH-ON` **(closed)** 2,447 · rulings-that-generalise 2,402 · CC-A errors 2,034 · `B-EPOCH-KEYING-PARITY` **(closed)** 1,950 · the board 1,606 · preamble 912 · comms 654 · ledger header 646.

**THE EASY CUT IS REAL BUT INSUFFICIENT.** Five CLOSED-batch sections total **12,920 B (26%)**, and STANDING NOTES carries ~4,600 B more of the same class on four single lines (`B-ARM-REMOVAL` **1,469 B on ONE line**, `P19-B8.5l` 1,117, `P19-B8.5h` 1,045, `B-TSC-BASELINE-FIX` 962). ★ **`CLAUDE.md` §3.2 already orders exactly this — collapse a closed batch to ONE line the moment it closes, because the completion report is the authoritative record.** ⇒ **collapsing all of it lands at ~32,000 B. STILL OVER.**

⛔⛔ **AND THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT THE ARITHMETIC: WHAT REMAINS AFTER THE EASY CUTS IS ~26,700 B OF THINGS THAT ALL LOOK LOAD-BEARING — AND IT EXCEEDS THE CAP BEFORE A SINGLE NEW LINE IS WRITTEN.** His reviewer ledger alone (retractions + generalising rulings + per-session error log + header) is **10,296 B**, and `B-REVIEWER-LOOP` **F2** counts those six retractions as load-bearing evidence. ⇒ **the cap cannot be met by trimming; either something changes structurally or the cap is wrong for this file.**

**THREE SHAPES PUT TO LANGSTON — HIS RULING, NOT MINE** (Kyle: *"work with Langston to understand what is necessary and what could be cut"*):

| | shape | the objection that decides it |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **the ledger MOVES to the repo** (`LANGSTON_REVIEWER_LEDGER.md`) with a pointer — frees ~9,000 B | ⛔ **its value is POSITIONAL: it works because it arrives BEFORE he reviews, without him remembering to fetch it. A pointer only fires if he goes and reads it — and he cannot be relied on to remember what he does not know he has forgotten.** Moving it may destroy the property that makes it work. |
| **B** | **compress in place** — each retraction to one line (claim / truth / error-class), reasoning to the repo | keeps the positional property, loses the narrative that makes a retraction legible as a *pattern* rather than an incident |
| **C** | ★ **the cap is wrong for HIM and we say so** | **he is STATELESS per-invoke — this file plus his `CLAUDE.md` IS his entire memory, where a CC session accumulates context across a long conversation. ### #635 OPEN 2026-07-31 (CC-B; Langston Step-4 required home, #594) — ★ THE xSTOCK STALL WATCHDOG DETECTS A **TOTAL** FEED STALL ONLY, AND ITS THRESHOLDS ARE UNCALIBRATED FOR THE AGGREGATE CLOCK IT NOW READS

★ **RULE 24 OUTCOME (2) — WORKING-AS-DESIGNED-BUT-UNADDRESSED. A SCOPE DECISION, NOT A DEFECT.** #594 correctly repointed the watchdog from an any-frame clock to a DATA clock. **Both are UNIVERSE-WIDE** — stamped once per symbol-tick across ~485 symbols ⇒ **one symbol going dark while 484 keep ticking leaves the clock reading FRESH.** The watchdog cannot see a PARTIAL stall and never could; #594 neither introduced nor fixed that.

⚠ **AND THE THRESHOLDS ARE FROM A DIFFERENT POPULATION — the correction that produced this entry.** `stall_reconnect_ms_rth = 75000` / `_offrth = 750000` were derived from **PER-SYMBOL successive `captured_at` diffs** (freshness doc §3, n=6.00M RTH / 1.15M off-RTH). The clock they now gate is **aggregate**: at ~900K-996K ticks/hr the inter-arrival is **~4ms**, against a **75s** threshold — **~4 orders of magnitude apart.** ⇒ **the numbers are not WRONG, they are UNCALIBRATED FOR THIS OBJECT.** ★ **What IS true and checkable, and is what #594 claims: the aggregate clock is STRICTLY DENSER than the per-symbol clock the constants came from ⇒ #594 CANNOT make the watchdog fire more often than before.** ⇒ **so #594 is SAFE without being calibrated, and this entry is the calibration question.**

**THE SCOPE DECISION FOR KYLE/LANGSTON:** should the watchdog detect **per-symbol** staleness (one dark name among many), and if so at what threshold? ⚠ **This bears on xStock ACTIVE-FILL enablement** — the fill path is freshness-gated per symbol, so a per-symbol stall is exactly the case a total-stall detector misses. **Related: #594, #636, #583.** **OPEN (homed, owner CC-B).**

★★ **MEASURED 2026-08-24 (CC-C, discharging alert `3543742c` — the per-symbol threshold question this entry has carried OPEN and UNMEASURED since 07-31).** Object: `xstock_spot_ticker_snap`, successive `captured_at` diffs **per symbol**, 24 h to 2026-08-24T10:05Z. Population: **436,350 gaps across 476 symbols.**

| | |
|---|---:|
| p50 gap | **5.5 s** |
| p90 | 35.7 s |
| p99 | **681.4 s** |
| max | 26,769 s (7.4 h) |
| gaps > 300 s (the exit ceiling `floor_ms`) | 8,833 = **2.02%** |
| **DISTINCT symbols with ≥1 gap > 300 s** | **476 of 476 — every single one** |

★ **THE ANSWER IS NOT "THE BOOK IS SLOW" — IT IS THAT THE TAIL IS UNIVERSAL.** The typical xStock quotes every **5.5 s**, comfortably inside any sane ceiling. But **every symbol in the book goes silent for more than 5 minutes at some point in a 24-hour day**, and 1% of intervals exceed **11 minutes**. ⇒ a per-symbol staleness detector thresholded anywhere near the p50 would fire on all 476 names; thresholded past the p99 it would miss the windows that matter. **That is the shape of the scope decision this entry asks for, now stated in numbers rather than intuition.**

⚠️ **THIS MEASUREMENT UNDERSTATES, BY CONSTRUCTION — #594's OWN LESSON APPLIED TO ITSELF.** A `lag`-based gap analysis **cannot see a TRAILING silence**: a symbol that went dark and STAYED dark has no subsequent row to close the interval, so it contributes **no gap at all** rather than a large one. The live `/api/xstocks/freshness` snapshot taken in the same minute shows **136 of 483 symbols in state `dead` and 169 `stale`** against the endpoint's own 90 s/600 s thresholds — a heavy standing tail that the gap distribution above is structurally blind to. **Treat 2.02% as a FLOOR on the exposure, never as the exposure.**

⚠️ **AND TWO STALENESS STANDARDS ARE LIVE ON ONE OBJECT (the #641 shape, flagged not fixed):** `/api/xstocks/freshness` calls a mark fresh up to **90 s**; the exit ceiling floors at **300 s**. Neither is wrong for its own purpose, but nothing reconciles them and a reader moving between the two surfaces gets different answers about the same symbol.

★ **WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* SHOW, stated so it is not read across:** the marks we DO act on are sound. The policy is fail-closed and refused every mark it could not trust — **no position was mispriced.** This is an availability-of-evaluation exposure (↔ **#563**), **not** a price-integrity one, and it does **not** belong to the `B-EXIT-PROVENANCE` price-correctness series.

### #636 OPEN 2026-07-31 (CC-B; Langston Step-4 required home, #594) — SNAP-ARRIVAL ≠ MARK-FRESHNESS: `lastDataMsgAt` CAN READ FRESH WHILE `latestEquityTick` AGES

★ **MECHANISM, CITED NOT MEASURED (rule 29c).** In `parseTickerSnap` the `!data?.symbol` guard is **unconditional**, but the mark write is **conditional** — `Number.isFinite(_mark) && _mark > 0`. ⇒ **a snap can pass the guard, be archived, stamp `lastDataMsgAt`, and write NO mark** ⇒ the DATA-liveness clock reads fresh while `latestEquityTick` — **the only venue price source for tokenized equities, consumed by `active-execution-engine.ts:141`** — goes stale.

⚠ **#594's STAMP PLACEMENT IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT MOVE TO “FIX” THIS:** stamping inside the mark branch would make `parseTickerSnap` inconsistent with `parseOhlcBar`, which has no mark at all. ⇒ **the answer is not relocating the stamp; it is deciding whether MARK-freshness needs its own detector.** ★ **NOT MEASURED: I have not established that a finite-symbol/non-finite-mark snap actually occurs in practice** — the mechanism exists in code; its frequency is unknown, and that measurement is the entry's first task. **Related: #594, #635.** **OPEN (homed, owner CC-B).**

★★ **MEASURED 2026-08-24 (CC-C, discharging alert `3543742c`) — THIS ENTRY'S "FIRST TASK" IS NOW DONE, AND THE ANSWER IS *ESSENTIALLY NEVER*.** Object: `xstock_spot_ticker_snap`, 24 h to 2026-08-24T10:05Z, `NULL`-safe bucketing (`COALESCE(...,0)` so a NULL cannot silently vanish from every bucket — a first pass without it left 2 rows in no bucket at all).

| bucket | rows |
|---|---:|
| snaps archived | **436,826** |
| mark from a live **bid/ask mid** | **436,824** |
| mark fell back to `last` | **2** |
| **wrote NO mark (the #636 case)** | **0** |

⇒ **the mechanism is REAL IN CODE and did not occur ONCE in 24 hours at 437 k snaps.** `parseTickerSnap`'s conditional mark write is reachable in principle; in practice the equities feed supplies a two-sided quote on **99.9995%** of snaps. **Do not spend a batch on it, and do NOT relocate the stamp** (this entry and #594 both already say why). ★ **A bonus this measurement settles:** the `last` fallback — a *carried-forward* print rather than a live quote — fired **twice**, so the mark is a live two-sided mid essentially always. That closes a fail-open worry I raised separately about `last` being economically stale while reading fresh: **not a live exposure on this path.**

⚠️ **POPULATION LIMIT, NAMED:** this counts snaps that WERE archived. `bufferTickerSnap` **throttles** per `assetClass:symbol`, so it is a throttled sample of arrivals, not every arrival — and a frame rejected by the `!data?.symbol` guard upstream never reaches the table. Neither can manufacture the `no_mark_written` case this bucket counts, so the **zero holds**; but the 437 k is a sample size, not a frame count.

### #660 OPEN 2026-08-07 (Kyle challenge on the B-TRADE-TIER-REGISTER summary; CC-A) — THE TRADE TABLES’ 365d HOT WINDOW WAS INHERITED FROM A DELETE-ERA DECISION AND WAS NEVER RE-ASKED NOW THAT AGING MEANS ARCHIVING

**Kyle’s question:** *"Why isn’t this going through the normal process of after 30 days, it goes into warm, then cold like all of the other data?"* **Answer measured at `module_constants.data_lifecycle`: there is NO universal 30d hot window** — 30d is the high-volume TICKER-SNAP window (`*_ticker_snap`); analytics tables (`signal_eval_archive`, `exit_decision_archive`, `pair_scan_archive`, `macro_feed_archive`, `signal_eval_provenance`, `switch_on_shadow_evidence`, `xstock_qd_probe_history`) use **90**; OHLC bar tables use **365**; `context_bridge_log` uses **14**. So the trade tables are not off-standard — but the NUMBER’s PROVENANCE is the real finding.
⚠ **THE GAP, owned: the 365 was Kyle’s own leg-1 decision (2026-07-30) taken when aging meant PERMANENT DELETION. B-TRADE-TIER-REGISTER changed aging to mean MOVE-TO-WARM — and I carried the number across WITHOUT re-asking whether it is still the right number under the new semantics.** A retention window chosen to protect data from deletion is not automatically the right window for when to relocate it.
****★ ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-07 (audit `LEARNING_AND_STORAGE_AUDIT_2026-08-07.md`): the trade tables are ~62 MB against a ~142 GB database = 0.04%. THE RETENTION WINDOW ON TRADES IS NOT A STORAGE QUESTION.** Hot storage is `signal_eval_archive` (~57 GB) + `xstock_spot_ticker_snap` (26 GB). **CC-A RECOMMENDATION: KEEP 365 for both trade tables** — a full year of trades stays instantly queryable for calibration/AMR work at a cost of ~0.04% of the database, and Phase-25 calibration (per `STRATEGIC_DIRECTIONS_AND_AI_EDGE.md`) is exactly the consumer that wants a long, uninterrupted trade history in hot. Shortening to 90 would save ~45 MB and cost the calibration phase its convenient window — a bad trade. **Revisit ONLY if the trade tables ever exceed ~1% of the DB.** THE DECISION (Kyle’s, options costed):** (a) KEEP 365 — a full year of trades instantly queryable in hot; largest live DB; (b) MOVE TO 90 — aligns with every other analytics table, shrinks the live DB materially, and the rows remain fully readable from warm (this batch proved the read-back path end-to-end); (c) something between. **Cold rotation is unaffected either way** — the rotator moves any warm object by source_table with the global 365d warm default, so trades roll warm→cold automatically with no further work. **HOME: this entry, owner CC-A; a one-line `module_constants` change + governance note once Kyle rules.** | OPEN (awaiting Kyle) |

### #647 OPEN 2026-08-01 (CC-C, endorsed independently by CC-A and CC-B) — ★★ **THE ALERT QUEUE IS A SHARED MUTABLE RESOURCE WITH NO CLAIM MECHANISM, AND TWO SESSIONS' ACTIONS ON ONE ROW CAN SILENTLY CANCEL EACH OTHER.**
**★ THIS IS THE FINDING THAT SURVIVED THE NIGHT'S FOUR-ERROR CASCADE, AND IT NEVER DEPENDED ON ANY OF IT.** #646 was retracted as false at the premise; **this stands on TWO TIMESTAMPS ALONE** and was re-endorsed by both peers *after* the retraction, unprompted. **Recorded separately for exactly that reason: a true finding filed inside a retracted entry gets thrown out with it.**
**★★ SEVERITY RAISED SAME DAY — SECOND COLLISION, 445 ms APART, AND THIS ONE PROVES THE RECORD IS LAST-WRITER-WINS: A LOSING ACTION IS ERASED, NOT MERELY CANCELLED.**
**Alert `f7c0d514` (`price-skip-paper-MCK/USD`).** CC-C resolved at **`23:06:31.417Z`**; CC-B resolved at **`23:06:31.862Z`** — **445 ms apart, neither aware.**
**PROOF THE FIRST WRITE WAS REAL AND IS NOW GONE (not a misread — this distinction was itself contested):** CC-C's read, issued in the same command as its own resolve, returned `resolved_by_claimed: cc-c`, `resolution_evidence: **f2a99ddbf**` — **the branch head CC-C computed locally and passed as `--evidence`; no other process held that value.** CC-B's line carries `evidence: #638`. **Two different evidence values ⇒ two distinct writes.** **`grep -c` on the id now returns `1`.** ⇒ **the earlier write is ABSENT — no second row, no conflict marker, no error.**
**★★ AND CC-B SETTLED IT STRUCTURALLY — a better proof than the single-row one above, and they produced it while RETRACTING their own correction of me: `system-alerts.jsonl` holds 482 lines and 482 DISTINCT ids — MAX ONE LINE PER ID.** ⇒ **the store is a SNAPSHOT, not a log, BY CONSTRUCTION.** **This is therefore not a property of one unlucky row: NO query on that store can EVER detect a superseded write, for ANY alert, because the prior version does not exist to be found.** ⇒ **the record does not merely fail to prevent a collision — it CONFIDENTLY REPORTS THE WRONG ACTOR, with no marker that anything was replaced.**
⇒ ★ **THE PROPERTY, corrected: this entry originally said two actions can "silently cancel". They can also SILENTLY ERASE. The ledger CANNOT be used to reconstruct who did what**, because the losing writer leaves nothing behind.
⚠️ **AND THE SECOND-ORDER COST IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER: IT MANUFACTURED A FALSE ACCUSATION BETWEEN SESSIONS.** CC-B correctly read the surviving row and concluded CC-C had repeated a known field error; **the only thing that refuted it was a hand-passed evidence value that happened to be unique.** **That will not usually be available.** ⇒ **an erasing record does not just lose data — it produces confident, well-reasoned, WRONG conclusions about colleagues.**
**★★ THE SYMMETRY CASE — 2026-08-01 00:07, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THIS ENTRY BECAUSE THE DIRECTION REVERSED.** Four alerts (`a0d7ca41` MCK · `732b73b4` PWR · `dcc7f24c` ETN · `6c14797a` PYPL). **CC-B resolved all four (`resolved_by_claimed: cc-b`, evidence `#646`) and verified them. CC-C then resolved all four at `00:07:02.393Z` / `:04.469` / `:06.717` / `:08.833` (`cc-c`, evidence `9c1dfdc42`) and verified them.** **Only CC-C's four survive; CC-B's are gone.**
⇒ ★ **At 23:06 CC-B erased CC-C by 445 ms. At 00:07 CC-C erased CC-B across four rows. NEITHER SESSION DID ANYTHING WRONG EITHER TIME, and BOTH verifications were CORRECT AT THE MOMENT TAKEN.** ⇒ **the store cannot distinguish *"I did this"* from *"I did this AND destroyed someone's identical action"* — and it produced a confident, evidence-backed WRONG accusation in BOTH directions.** **Recording the case where CC-C is the ERASER, not the victim: a defect only reported by the party it happened *to* is too easily read as a grievance.**
**⚠️ NET EFFECT ON THE ALERTS: ZERO — all four are correctly resolved and stay resolved. The damage is confined to the RECORD OF WHO ACTED.**
**⛔ AND A NEAR-MISS I ALMOST FILED AS A SUCCESS — CC-A CAUGHT IT, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE.** CC-A announced a claim on all four *before* acting, and I was about to record that as evidence that **announce-before-acting works as a mitigation (n=3)**. **IT IS NOT WHAT HAPPENED: CC-A's four resolves were NO-OPS — their id extraction produced EMPTY ids — so the collision was averted by a SILENTLY FAILING COMMAND, not by the announcement.** ⇒ **filing it as a working mitigation would have put a FALSE LESSON in a durable place, which is precisely this entry's own subject.**
**⛔⛔ AND CC-B CORRECTED EVEN THAT — THE HARSHER VERSION IS THE TRUE ONE, AND IT SUPERSEDES THE 'near-miss' FRAMING ABOVE: THE COLLISION WAS NOT AVOIDED. IT HAD ALREADY COMPLETED.** CC-A posted *"claiming all four BEFORE I touch them"* and CC-B posted *"stop, drop all four"* — **but `cc-c` had ALREADY overwritten all four at `00:07`, silently, before either message was written.** ⇒ **the claim-before-acting convention worked on the session that ASKED; it did nothing whatever about the write that had already landed.** ⇒ ★ **the tally is n=4 COMPLETED OVERWRITES in one evening, NOT n=3 near-misses — and it was discovered ONLY by three sessions comparing notes afterwards, which is not a control and does not scale.** **The announcement remains good practice and is NOT evidenced as protective — it cannot be, since it fires after the write it would have to prevent. Do not cite it as a mitigation.**
**BOTH collisions were on the SAME alert class within ONE HOUR: 20.4 s and 445 ms.** ⇒ **n=2, and the interval is shrinking as more sessions adopt resolve-never-ack — which the interim rule actively encourages.**
**THE EVIDENCE — two fields on one row, `b112a58d`:** `acknowledged_at = 2026-07-31T22:06:28.777Z` (CC-C) · `resolved_at = 2026-07-31T22:06:49.148Z` (CC-B, `resolved_by_claimed: cc-b`). **20.371 seconds apart. Neither session knew the other was acting.**
**★ WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A COINCIDENCE — THE TWO ACTIONS PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.** `system-alerts.ts:389` suppresses a fresh raise while a same-`dedupe_key` alert is `state !== 'resolved'`, and **`acknowledged` is NON-TERMINAL** ⇒ **an ACK SUPPRESSES future occurrences; a RESOLVE FREES them.** ⇒ **one of the two actions was silently SUBTRACTIVE.** Had CC-B not resolved 20s later, **CC-C's ack — performed in compliance with §10.5 as written — would have left PYPL's exit-skip condition suppressed indefinitely.** **Neither session did anything wrong; the queue has no way to tell them they were both there.**
**★ THE STRUCTURAL STATEMENT: rule 25.a's crew board claims PATHS. The alert queue is EQUALLY shared, EQUALLY mutable, and has NO claim mechanism at all.** Same class as two sessions editing one file — **minus the tool that catches it.** ⇒ **the board's own honesty clause (25.b) applies here with more force: what does not exist cannot be forgotten to be used.**
**⚠️ AND IT COMPOUNDS WITH THE INTERIM RESOLVE-NEVER-ACK RULE (Langston, #638):** that rule makes RESOLVE the correct action on self-clearing classes, so **more sessions will now be writing terminal state to the same rows** — the collision surface grows, not shrinks, until something coordinates it.
**⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED:** the frequency (**one observed instance — n=1**); whether any REAL suppression has occurred in production (**unmeasured — nobody has counted acked-not-resolved rows against their dedupe keys**); or that a claim mechanism is the right fix rather than, say, making ack terminal-by-default on self-clearing classes. **The gap is established; the remedy is not.**
**HOME (§9.4): the alert-integrity workstream already in flight — `#637(2)` / `#638`, owner CC-B**, because the ack/resolve semantics being changed there are the same surface. **A concrete first step that needs no design decision: COUNT the acked-not-resolved rows and how many dedupe keys they are currently suppressing** — that converts "this could happen" into a measured exposure. ### #646 ⛔ **RETRACTED BY ITS AUTHOR 2026-08-01, WITHIN THE HOUR, AS FALSE AT THE PREMISE — struck, NOT deleted, because the retraction is the record.** (CC-C; CC-B caught it)
**⛔ THE DEFECT CLAIMED BELOW DOES NOT EXIST. `resolved_by` IS NOT A NULL FIELD — IT IS NOT A FIELD.** Keys ENUMERATED (not guessed) on row `b112a58d`: `acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, body, category, created_at, dedupe_key, fired_at, id, metadata, recurrence_interval_seconds, resolution_evidence, resolved_at, **resolved_by_claimed**, **resolved_by_transport**, schema_version, severity, state, title, triggers_at`. **`'resolved_by' in d → False.`**
**THE ACTOR WAS FULLY RECORDED ALL ALONG: `resolved_by_claimed = 'cc-b'`, `resolved_by_transport = 'cli'`.** ⇒ **there is no asymmetry between the ack and resolve paths, the ledger CAN say who closed it, and every consequence I drew from the "null" is void.**
**★ HOW I PRODUCED IT, stated plainly because it is the only part with value: I ran `d.get('resolved_by')`, got `None` BECAUSE THE KEY DOES NOT EXIST, and read a MISSING KEY as a NULL VALUE.** ⇒ **`.get()` cannot distinguish "absent" from "present-and-null", and I never enumerated the keys to find out which I had.** **That is rule 25.c — a matching name is not a matching thing — and #627's incomplete-control lesson, in one line of Python.**

### #645 OPEN 2026-08-01 (CC-C, Kyle-hypothesised and CONFIRMED) — ★★ **THE NET-EV FLOOR IS ONE HARDCODED CONSTANT CALIBRATED IN THE CRYPTO ERA AND LATER *EXPORTED* TO xSTOCK RATHER THAN RE-DERIVED.** Kyle: *"Is there a threshold that we've just blindly been using for both?"* — **yes, and the code comment says so.**

Active trading unaffected (strict netEV>0). B79.0m.b2: exported for xstock eval-cycle."***
⇒ **calibrated at Batch 52, when crypto was effectively the only class; the xStock path consumes the SAME symbol by import** (`server/asset_classes/xstock_spot/eval-cycle.ts:63` imports it, `:793` gates on it, `:833` stamps it). **The word in the comment is "exported", not "re-derived" — the sharing is documented as a plumbing act, not a calibration decision.**
**★ AND IT IS NOT A FEE ASYMMETRY — ruled out by measurement.** `module_constants.fee_model`: `spot_taker_fee = 0.008` and `spot_maker_fee = 0.004` for **BOTH** `crypto_spot` and `xstock_spot`. **Identical.** ⇒ the observed split (crypto fills the exploration lane, xStock trades organically — #644) is **not** crypto paying more to trade.

**NEXT STEP (bounded):** per-class realised friction vs realised gross move, computed so the identity is preserved (ratio-of-sums, not mean-of-ratios — the likely defect in my attempt), split organic vs exploration. **That distinguishes "the floor is mis-set for crypto" from "crypto's friction estimate is too pessimistic".**

### #634 OPEN 2026-07-31 (filed by CC-C · **OWNER: CC-B**, Langston-assigned) — ★ **THE DAILY-LOSS EVALUATOR'S FAILURE COUNTER HAS ZERO READERS: when the kill-switch evaluation throws, it is counted and logged — and NOTHING SURFACES IT.** ⚠️ **AND THIS ENTRY CORRECTS MY OWN FIRST DESCRIPTION OF IT.**
**⚠️ WHAT I SAID FIRST, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG.** On finding the error I described the catch as a **silent swallow / fail-open** and said *"no one is told."* **Reading the code refutes the first half.** `recordEvalFailure` (`daily-loss-budget.ts:213-218`) **increments a per-mode counter AND `console.error`s**, under a section header that reads verbatim **`// ─── Observable failure counter (Langston/rule-11: no silent swallow) ───`.** ⇒ **it was DELIBERATELY built not to be silent, at Langston's instruction. Reporting it as a silent swallow would have impugned work that was done correctly** — §9.5(b-ii), and rule 24.a's *read the intent before you name the cause.*
**★ THE REAL DEFECT IS ONE LAYER OUT, AND IT IS NARROWER AND MORE PRECISE: THE OBSERVABILITY IS UNREACHABLE.** PRESENCE-EVIDENCE, whole repo, nothing excluded — `grep -rn "getDailyLossEvalStats" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` returns **EXACTLY ONE LINE: its own definition at `:217`.** **No route, no diagnostic panel, no alert, no test.** ⇒ the counter faithfully accumulates a number **that no code path can ever read**, and the only surviving trace of a failed kill-switch evaluation is a `console.error` line in a log nobody watches.
**⇒ THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, STATED CAREFULLY.** A throw anywhere inside `compute24hSnapshot` — the guardrail read, the balance read, the realized-P&L read — means **that evaluation contributes nothing: no tier, no trip, no warning.** The evaluator is invoked per trade CLOSE, so a persistent fault means **the daily-loss kill switch stops evaluating entirely while the system keeps trading, and the only signal is a log line.** **Direction is fail-OPEN on a risk boundary.**
**★ FIFTH INSTANCE OF THE SESSION'S RUNNING PATTERN — correct behaviour built, then left unreachable:** `getClosedTradesGlobal` (0 callers) · `dbNetPnl` (never passed) · `updateClosedTrade`'s returned row (discarded) · `calculateRiskAmount`'s zero-guard (defeated upstream) · **and now an observability counter with no reader.** **Five is not a coincidence; the deliberate sweep proposed at the fourth is overdue.**
**HOW IT SURFACED (worth keeping):** not by audit — **by my own regression.** My `B-KILLSWITCH-WINDOW` hotfix broke `p19-b6-daily-loss-budget.integration.test.ts` (its storage mock lacked `getRealizedPnlSince`), and the failure printed as `[DailyLossBudget] evaluation error (paper): … is not a function` **rather than failing loudly.** ⇒ **the fault I introduced was ALSO a live demonstration of the fault being filed.**
**⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, do not assert from this entry:** that any real evaluation has EVER thrown in production (**unmeasured — the counter is unreadable and stdout retention is short**); or that a trip was missed. **What is established is reachability, not incidence.**
**★★ LANGSTON RULING 2026-07-31 — OWNER CORRECTED TO CC-B, AND A DIRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE HOMING.**
- **OWNER: CC-B**, not CC-C as I first filed it. Titled as the risk-boundary fail-open on `computeDailyLossVerdict`. **Rule-24 bucket (2) — working-as-designed-but-unaddressed: the try/catch is DELIBERATE fault isolation, so this is a SCOPE DECISION, not a defect, and not mine to fix inside the hotfix.**
- **⚠️⚠️ DO NOT MAKE IT THROW — flagged by Langston precisely so nobody sprints the wrong way.** *"An evaluator that trips the kill on a transient DB blip flattens the book, which is the worse failure."* ⇒ **the naive "fail closed on a risk boundary" instinct is WRONG here**, and this line exists to stop it being applied on sight.
- **THE CANDIDATE: surface CONSECUTIVE failures — the counter already exists, it just needs a reader and an alert** (mirroring the consecutive-refusal rail P19-B8.8 built for the sizer). **The behaviour choice is KYLE'S because it moves risk.**
- **He also confirms it is slightly WORSE than I stated:** the only surviving trace is a `console.error` on **stdout, which rotates on staging in about two days** — so even the log is gone within 48h.

**ORIGINAL HOMING (SUPERSEDED by the ruling above — kept because the reasoning still applies to the fix's shape):** fold into the **`#618` denominator batch** — same function, same file, one edit to wire the counter to the existing system-alerts path — **or its own small batch if #618's denominator leg is not scoped soon. Owner: CC-C.** **Fix shape:** surface `getDailyLossEvalStats` (route or the existing alert dispatcher) and **raise a system alert on consecutive failures**, mirroring the consecutive-refusal rail P19-B8.8 built for the sizer. **NOT folded into the `B-KILLSWITCH-WINDOW` hotfix** — that batch is Langston-APPROVED at `8032ca02f` and this is a behaviour addition, not its bug. | OPEN


### #633 OPEN 2026-07-31 (CC-C) — ★★ **THE TARGET-GOAL SAFETY CHECK CANNOT FAIL: it reads TWO guardrail fields that DO NOT EXIST on the response, falls back to fabricated values, and computes a warn threshold ABOVE 100%.** It gates a save button and persists a verdict.
**SURFACED BY THE A10 CLIENT CENSUS** (which was itself required because I once asserted *"the only one left"* about this pattern with no census and had to withdraw it).
**★ PRESENCE-EVIDENCE, NOT INFERENCE (rule 22 — an asserted absence needs presence-evidence).** LIVE call to `GET /api/guardrails?mode=paper` on staging returns exactly these keys: `id, mode, portfolioRiskPerTradePct, symbolCooldownMinutes, maxOpenPositions, dailyLossKillSwitchPct, dailyLossWarning1Pct, dailyLossWarning2Pct, maxPositionPercentPct, maxTotalExposurePct, lowPriceMinStopAtrMult, lowPriceMinPositionNotional, lowPriceThreshold, isManualOverride, tunedByLatti, lockedByUser, managedByLottie, manualOverrideEnabled, lastUpdatedBy, killSwitchTripped, killSwitchReason, killSwitchTrippedAt, lastUpdated`.
| client reads (`target-daily-goals.tsx`) | on the response? | result |
|---|---|---|
| `guardrailsData.dailyLossKillSwitch` (`:145`) | **ABSENT** (the real key is `dailyLossKillSwitchPct` = **20**) | falls back to **`'5000'`** |
| `guardrailsData.maxDailyLoss` (`:144`) | **ABSENT** | falls back to **`'1000'`** — **and then is NEVER USED AGAIN** (dead assignment, rule 18 / §15 candidate) |
**★ THE ARITHMETIC, AND IT IS ROBUST — the check is structurally incapable of warning at our size.** `:148` `safeLimit = (dailyLossKillSwitch / portfolioBalance) * 100 * 5`. With the fabricated 5000 this is **`2,500,000 / B` percent**. ⇒ **`safeLimit ≥ 100%` for ANY portfolio `B ≤ $25,000`.** Ours is **≈$2,250 ⇒ safeLimit ≈ 1,111%**, `blockThreshold ≈ 2,222%`. The ladder is `targetPct <= warnThreshold → 'OK'` (`:152-156`). **A daily target is realistically 1-10%. No such value can ever reach WARN, let alone BLOCK.**
**⚠️ NOT COSMETIC — the always-'OK' verdict is load-bearing in three places:** `:333` it **gates the Save button** (`disabled={… || validationResult?.status === 'BLOCK'}`) ⇒ **that gate can never engage**; `:228-231` a BLOCK toast ⇒ **unreachable**; `:197-201` the verdict is **PERSISTED to the server** as `feasibilityStatus` / `validationMessage` / `riskLimit` / `exceedsBy` ⇒ **every saved target is recorded as feasible with `exceedsBy: '0'`, regardless of how aggressive it is.**
**PROVENANCE (§2 1.b / rule 24.0) — THE FORMULA WAS WRITTEN FOR A FIELD THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, AND THE UNITS PROVE IT.** Dividing by `portfolioBalance` only makes sense for an **absolute currency** kill switch; the legacy `guardrails.maxDailyLoss` is exactly that (`schema.ts:285`, `decimal(10,2) default "1000.00"` — **note the default matches the client's `'1000'` fallback**). The current SoT is **percent-based** `guardrails_v2.dailyLossKillSwitchPct` (`:325`). ⇒ **the guardrails migration to `_v2` changed the units and the key; this component was left behind, and its `||` fallbacks absorbed the break silently** — no error, no undefined render, just a number.
**★ RULE-24 DISPOSITION: OUTCOME 3 (legacy that no longer fits) WITH AN OUTCOME-1 CONSEQUENCE (a safety check that cannot fail).** Not a coding mistake in its own era — a survivor of a migration.
**LEDGER CHECK DONE (§9.5 b-ii) — RELATED TO #400 BUT NOT A DUPLICATE.** **#400** names **two SERVER-side legacy-guardrail callers** (`reasoning-orchestrator.ts:500`, `intent-executor.ts:418`) reading the old table. **This is a THIRD site, on the CLIENT, reading the old ENDPOINT's old SHAPE** — same family, different artifact. Recorded separately and cross-linked rather than folded in, because #400's fix (re-point two server reads) would **not** touch this file.
**⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, do not assert from this entry:** that any TRADE was mis-sized or mis-risked (this is the goal-setting surface, not the sizing path — contrast **#628**, where I wrongly claimed a sizing impact and corrected it); or that any downstream consumer acts on the persisted `feasibilityStatus` (**untraced — nobody has enumerated its readers**).
**HOME (§9.4): fold into the `#400` legacy-guardrails retirement batch** (the units + key + dead assignment are one edit), **owner CC-C**, or its own small batch if #400 is not scheduled soon. **Fix shape: read `dailyLossKillSwitchPct` and drop the divide-by-balance; delete the dead `maxDailyLoss` line; and make the absence LOUD rather than defaulted** — a safety check whose inputs are missing must refuse, not pass. | OPEN

### #629 OPEN 2026-07-31 (Langston-found, filed by CC-A at his instruction) — ★★ A RE-SURFACING ALERT RE-EMITS ITS **FIRST-FIRE** MEASUREMENT INSTEAD OF RE-MEASURING — A STALE GAUGE PRESENTED AS CURRENT STATE
**HOME: its own row under the #623 family, owner CC-A.** ⚠ **Langston explicitly REFUSED my proposal to "fold it into `B-MEASURE-GATE`":** *"§13: 'folding it into B-MEASURE-GATE' isn't a home. Put it in `RUNNING_ISSUES` as its own row … because that's a distinct mechanism from the measure-time gate and it'll get lost inside leg 2's hooks work otherwise."* **He is right and the correction is recorded rather than quietly accepted.**

**THE DEFECT, measured:** the disk-critical alert `65272303` re-surfaced **four times** — each time re-stating its **FIRST-FIRE** reading of **166.4 GB / 83.2%** from two days earlier. **Langston re-measured the database directly and it was 172.25 GB / 86.1%**; CC-A then independently confirmed **184,962,780,307 bytes = 172.27 GiB = 86.1%** at 2026-07-31T01:35:48Z. ⇒ **the alert under-reported a CRITICAL, MONOTONICALLY-GROWING condition by ~6 GB / ~3 percentage points, and did so more confidently each time it re-fired.**

★★ **WHY THIS IS ITS OWN CLASS AND NOT A COSMETIC BUG: a re-surface is an ASSERTION ABOUT NOW.** A human or session reading *"RE-SURFACE #4 — STILL UNRESOLVED: 83.2%"* reasonably reads 83.2% as the CURRENT figure — there is nothing in the message saying the number is historical. ⇒ **an instrument reporting its own history as current state**, which is the same failure family as `B-MEASURE-GATE` (#623) but at a **different point in the pipeline**: the gate governs how a session MEASURES; this is the ALERTING LAYER measuring once and then repeating itself. **Rule 29(b) says silence is not evidence until the instrument is shown able to speak; this is the sibling case — a NUMBER is not evidence until the instrument is shown to have re-read it.**
⚠ **AND THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS THE DANGEROUS ONE.** For any growing resource the stale figure is always **BETTER than reality**, so the alert **systematically understates urgency, and understates it more the longer it goes unresolved.** A decision to defer, taken on a re-surfaced reading, is taken on the most optimistic number available.

**CANDIDATE FIX (not yet designed — do not treat as scope):** a re-surfacing alert either **re-runs its measurement before re-emitting**, or **labels the figure with its as-of timestamp** so a reader can see it is historical. The first is correct; the second is the cheap fallback where re-measurement is expensive or unsafe. **Whichever is chosen, "83.2%" must never appear again without an as-of stamp.**
★ **Also worth checking in the same batch — NOT verified, stated as an open question:** whether OTHER re-surfacing alert classes share the mechanism (this was found on one alert; the census across alert types has not been run, and asserting it is only-this-one would need presence-evidence). | OPEN — own row, owner CC-A, #623 family | Found by Langston during triage of `65272303` 2026-07-31; his correction of the filing location recorded above.

### #160 OPEN 2026-05-28 — TFS confidence-formula `momentumFactor` saturates above 1% xStock momentum (Phase 25 calibration input)
B-XSTOCK-CALIB B.1a archive replay (2,658 bars / 260 symbols) surfaced a structural characteristic of the TFS confidence formula on xStock data. The formula `confidence = tfsDesatMin + (tfsDesatMax - tfsDesatMin) × (momentumFactor × dbsStrength × volInverse)` computes `momentumFactor = clamp01(mom / tfsMomentumScale)` with xstock_spot's `tfsMomentumScale = 0.010`. So momentumFactor saturates at 1.0 once raw momentum exceeds 1%. xStock momentum p95 from the replay = 6.0%, so the saturation point is well below the 95th percentile of TFS-eligible bars. Practical effect: for the bulk of TFS-classified xStock bars, the formula's dynamic range collapses to `dbsStrength × volInverse` only — momentum is at the ceiling and not contributing to confidence differentiation. **Not a B.1 bug, not a B.1 fix** — the multiplicative formula structure with these scale values is intentional ("all three inputs must align" per B67.3.5 design). Phase 25 calibration cycle (when paper-trade outcomes are available) is the correct loop to decide whether momentumFactor saturation hurts trade selection — if high-confidence TFS labels predict winning trades only weakly, formula rescaling for xStock becomes justified at that point. Until then, capture as a structural observation. Full analysis in `Claude Comms and Packages/Cross-Session Briefs/B_1A_DISTRIBUTION_ANALYSIS.md` §2.1 + §5 Phase-25-handoff. | OPEN — Phase 25 calibration input | Surfaced 2026-05-28 during B-XSTOCK-CALIB B.1a archive replay.
